work.text: A fine-tuned robot control model, uploaded whole to Hugging Face. Miners start from the season's base model (LingBot-VLA 2.0 for simulation since 2026-09-01), train it by any recipe, publish the complete merged checkpoint, pay a fee in TAO, and announce the Hugging Face commit on chain. Every submitted model is public and free to download.
work.quote: publish their fine-tunes as complete model checkpoints on Hugging Face

scoring.text: A benchmark worker runs each checkpoint through LIBERO manipulation tasks in the MuJoCo simulator, seeded from the commitment's block hash plus a drand beacon. The score is the average success rate. Ranking is king-of-the-hill: a challenger takes the crown only if its score exceeds the champion's by more than 0.01; a tie loses and the challenger is left off the board. The evaluation code is in a separate repository.
scoring.quote: the challenge succeeds only if challenger_score > champion_score + champion_margin (default 0.01)
scoring.disagrees: The overview at the pinned commit says the round scores six LIBERO suites for a pi0.5 base; the live competitions API on 2026-09-19 names the simulation benchmark libero_pro_custom_1 with a LingBot-VLA 2.0 base and a baseline of 0.285833 over 5 trials.

split.text: Three pools. Simulation takes 15 percent of the miner share and pays only its top three at 70, 20 and 10 percent of that. Each of two real-robot tracks on an xArm 6 takes 42.5 percent, settled once a season: 95 percent to the single champion vested over 120 days, 5 percent shared by entries clearing the qualification bar. Live weights on 2026-09-19 read 0.425, 0.425, 0.105, 0.03, 0.015.
split.quote: relative weights 70 / 20 / 10 within the simulation track's 15% emission allocation

judges.text: Nine validators were active on the 2026-09-09 chain snapshot, of 64 permitted. Weights are committed then revealed, at most once per 100 blocks. Validators do not run the benchmark: validator.py reads a settled weight vector from the operator's backend API with a read-only key, normalizes it and calls set_weights. The evaluation itself runs on the operator's benchmark workers.
judges.quote: commit_reveal_weights_enabled True, weights_rate_limit 100, max_validators 64; chain-2026-09-09.json active_validators 9

cadence.text: Emission settles every 360 blocks, about 72 minutes. The validator's default is to set weights every 720 minutes. The simulation board turns per submission: a checkpoint is scored when it reaches the front of the queue and the champion holds until beaten. Real-robot tracks run as seasons of roughly a month, with fixed submission and evaluation windows. A new registration is immune for 5,000 blocks, about 16 hours.

buyer.text: Nobody is named. The front page describes a competition whose winning model becomes the next base, and every checkpoint is public on Hugging Face. The competitions API lists fees paid by miners, 0.1 TAO burned for simulation and 1.5 TAO transferred for a real track, and no price for anyone else. No customer, product or usage figure was found on the site, in the API or in the repository.
buyer.quote: Fine-tune the base model, submit your weights on-chain, and the best model becomes the next base.

exploits.text: The overview records a red-team study: the four base LIBERO suites could be saturated for about $50 of GPU time by memorizing public demonstrations, so two swap-perturbation suites were added. Other named attacks and answers: queue flooding, met by the burn fee and one commitment per hotkey per round; copying the champion, met by the tie-loses margin; resubmitting another miner's weights, met by shard fingerprinting; replayed burns, a 10-block window.
exploits.quote: the four base suites alone could be saturated for roughly $50 of GPU time by memorizing public demonstrations
